items.headline: City offers rebates for rooftop solar this spring
items.body: Households can apply for a rebate covering up to 30% of panel installation. Applications open Monday. The program is funded from the existing energy-efficiency line, not a new tax.

items.headline: River gauge hits seasonal high after weekend rain
items.body: The west fork crested overnight but stayed below flood stage. Parks along the bank remain open. Forecasters expect levels to ease by Thursday.

items.headline: Pilot bus lane cuts commute times on Route 7
items.body: A three-month trial reserved one lane at peak hours. Average trip time dropped 11 minutes. The board will vote next month on whether to keep it.

items.headline: Overnight lows stay above 70 for a fifth straight day
items.body: Warm nights have kept cooling demand high. The utility asked customers to shift laundry and dishes to midday. No rolling outages are planned.

items.headline: Saturday tree planting fills the last river-park plots
items.body: Volunteers put in 40 saplings before noon. Watering is on a two-week rotation. The city asked neighbors not to tie banners to the stakes.

items.headline: Hawks take the cup on a last-minute header
items.body: Maya Chen scored in stoppage time to finish 2–1. The visitors had equalized in the 80th. Fans spilled onto the concourse; no injuries were reported.

items.headline: Rookie point guard named starter for Friday
items.body: Jordan Hale will open against Eastside after three games off the bench. The coach cited ball pressure, not scoring. Tip-off is 7 p.m.

items.headline: County meet: 800-meter record falls by half a second
items.body: Lina Ortiz ran 2:05.1, breaking a mark that stood since 2014. Wind was legal. She said the plan was even splits, not a kick.

items.headline: Star striker listed day-to-day with ankle sprain
items.body: Imaging showed no fracture. The club expects a decision after Wednesday's training. The next fixture is Saturday at home.

items.headline: Relay team clips the regional mark by two tenths
items.body: The medley finished in 3:42.8. Officials confirmed the touchpads. The squad travels to sectionals next weekend.

items.headline: Transit app login fails for two hours, then returns
items.body: A certificate renewal stalled sign-in between 6 and 8 a.m. Tickets bought in that window were still valid. The vendor posted a postmortem.

items.headline: Libraries add evening wifi hours after student survey
items.body: Branches will keep the network on until 9 p.m. on weeknights. No staffed desk after close. The change starts next Monday.

items.headline: School district asks families to turn on 2FA this week
items.body: A phishing wave last month targeted parent portals. The district will require an authenticator app by Friday. Paper backup codes are available at the office.

items.headline: City publishes pothole reports as a weekly spreadsheet
items.body: The file lists street, ward, and days-to-fill. It will update every Friday noon. A map view is planned for later this year.

items.headline: Library hosts a laptop repair clinic this Thursday
items.body: Slots are 20 minutes. Bring the charger. Volunteers will not recover data from cracked drives.

items.headline: Neighbors pick a river mural from three finalists
items.body: Voting is open at the rec center through Sunday. The winning design goes on the floodwall in June. All three artists are local.

items.headline: Friday night market adds a second music stage
items.body: Food stalls stay in the usual lot. The new stage faces the river path. Organizers asked visitors to use the garage, not side streets.

items.headline: Saturday book club switches to a mystery this month
items.body: Copies are on the hold shelf. Discussion is 11 a.m. in the glass room. New readers are welcome; no signup required.

items.headline: High school drama opens a two-weekend run of Our Town
items.body: Shows are 7 p.m. Friday and Saturday. Student tickets are five dollars at the door. The auditorium is the old gym, not the new hall.

items.headline: Community choir sings on the courthouse steps at dusk
items.body: The program is 45 minutes and free. Bring a chair if you want one. The last bus downtown leaves at 9:10.
